title: The Price of Fidelity
text:
Translators of literary works face a dilemma that rarely troubles other writers: they must reproduce a text whose meaning is inseparable from its sound. A pun that delights readers in one language may collapse into mere nonsense when rendered word for word. Consequently, many translators accept that some effects are lost and concentrate on preserving the atmosphere the original creates.

The most accomplished versions, however, often compensate for these losses by inventing new equivalents elsewhere in the text. Such compensation is rarely noticed by readers, yet it reveals the translator's sensitivity to the author's voice. Critics therefore evaluate a translation not by counting its faithful sentences but by judging whether the whole work still feels alive.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what is the source of the translators' dilemma?
options: A text whose meaning is inseparable from its sound
A lack of dictionaries for rare languages
Pressure from publishers to shorten the text
Readers who refuse to accept any translation

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do the most accomplished versions often do?
options: Invent new equivalents elsewhere in the text
Follow the original sentence structure exactly

questions.text: Why are the compensations described in the second paragraph rarely noticed by readers?
options: Because they succeed in making the translation feel like the original
Because they are placed only in the footnotes
Because readers do not care about the author's voice
Because they contradict the original meaning

questions.text: What does the passage imply about how critics should judge a translation?
options: By counting how many sentences match the original
By whether the whole work still feels alive
By the length of the translated text
By the number of puns it preserves

vocabulary.definition: impossible to divide or separate from something else
a situation in which a difficult choice must be made between alternatives
to make up for a loss or lack by providing something else
the mood or feeling created by a place, work or situation

paragraph_translations: Los traductores de obras literarias se enfrentan a un dilema que rara vez preocupa a otros escritores: deben reproducir un texto cuyo significado es indisoluble de su sonido. Un juego de palabras que deleita a los lectores en un idioma puede convertirse en puro sinsentido al traducirse palabra por palabra. En consecuencia, muchos traductores aceptan que algunos efectos se pierden y concentran sus esfuerzos en conservar el ambiente que crea el original.

Sin embargo, las versiones más logradas suelen compensar esas pérdidas inventando nuevos equivalentes en otras partes del texto. Tal compensación rara vez la advierten los lectores, aunque revela la sensibilidad del traductor hacia la voz del autor. Por eso, los críticos evalúan una traducción no por contar sus frases fieles, sino por juzgar si la obra entera todavía se siente viva.
